name: Seat recliner sliding layer
application: Automotive seat recliner pivot bearing -- a closed-gap ring bearing, greased and covered by a welded lid, replacing PTFE-based PRO100E with a PFAS-free material at a fraction of the cost. Benchmarked against PRO100E, OILES Drymet LF and GGB DU. Target: EU OEM seating systems, low sliding speed (oscillatory, not continuous rotation), Tier-1 performance at roughly a 2x cost reduction versus PRO100E.

compliance.prompt_text: PFAS/PTFE-free is a HARD compliance filter when the requirements state it, not a soft preference. Every material's supplied data includes `contains_fluoropolymer_or_pfas` on its `materials`/`coatings`/`lubricants` entries. If the requirements specify a PFAS-free or PTFE-free constraint: do not place a material flagged `contains_fluoropolymer_or_pfas=true` into `ranked_materials` as a compliant top recommendation. You may still mention it in `gaps` or `design_brief` as "the best-performing option in the corpus, but disqualified by the PFAS-free requirement" if that's genuinely useful context -- but set `pfas_free_compliant="no"` on it and do not rank it alongside compliant candidates. Set `pfas_free_compliant="yes"` only for materials whose relevant source entries are NOT flagged `contains_fluoropolymer_or_pfas=true`; use `"unclear"` if the underlying data doesn't specify.

envelope: Automotive seat recliner pivot bearing: a closed-gap ring, greased and sealed under a welded lid (not dry-sliding) -- the grease is part of the design, the requirement is that it stays contained by the lid rather than migrating onto the seat's upholstered surfaces. Low sliding speed, oscillatory movement (not continuous rotation). Target coefficient of friction ~0.04-0.07 in the greased condition, with a similar static/dynamic friction gap and wear resistance to PRO100E -- static/dynamic friction transition (stick-slip) matters as much as steady-state friction, since that's the primary driver of audible squeak. Load capability at least 400 N/mm2 static / 200 N/mm2 dynamic, deformation under load under 5 micrometers. Must survive 600C for under a minute without damage or delamination (welding the bearing's back metal to the housing, plus possible e-painting) -- that's a manufacturing/assembly heat spike, not a continuous operating temperature. Target material thickness around 1.0mm (existing options span 0.5-1.5mm). Multi-year, maintenance-free service life. Cost is a first-order requirement, not just a tiebreaker: current PRO100E-based parts cost roughly 17.68 euro-cents, and the target is a variable cost at or below 0.08 euro/pc -- over a 50% reduction -- so a technically excellent but expensive candidate is not automatically the right answer here.
